text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
-- Britain's GEC candidate to bid for Thomson-CSF, government to decide on offers on April 7.
-- Finance Ministry expects some 120,000 job creations for 1997.
-- Banking sector strike tomorrow against planned reform of a 1937 decree controlling branch opening hours and staff work hours.
LA TRIBUNE
-- Junior doctors and hospital staff opposed to planned government controls on health spending to demonstrate in Paris today.
-- French and Germans to compete for location of assembly plant for future Airbus jumbo A3XX.
-- Dassault to buy nine percent stake in Gemplus.
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux board approves planned merger with Suez, but BNP which holds 7.19 percent of Suez voting rights remains reluctant.
L'AGEFI
-- French economists expect investments to pick up.
-- Food group Brioche Pasquier expects a slow growth for 1997.
-- French corporate treasurers' association chairman says in an interview the prices of banking services ought to be re-considered when the country switches to the euro.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- The fact that GEC is candidate to bid for Thomson-CSF is not an "unfriendly" move, says Lagardere chairman Noel Forgeard.
-- Air France Europe staff plans labour unrest for Friday.
-- Digital-TV bouquet AB-Sat chairman Claude Berda says in an interview has an investment margin of some 600 million francs, sets a target of 75,000 subscribers.
LIBERATION (Economic section)

-- Finance Minister Jean Arthuis expects economic pickup to gain momentum in 1997, does not rule out a 1997 growth rate higher than the forecast 2.3 percent. Cuts in unemployment rate are not expected soon however, since active population is expected to grow faster than job creations through 1997.
